## Description {#details}

The pair of uninitialised pointers to the <b>next</b> and <b>previous</b> list elements and the methods to access the pointers are inherited from the base class.

It is expected that instances of this class to be statically allocated in the <b>bss</b> section and cleared (set to zero) during startup.

These peculiar types of lists are used by registrars, to automate the self-registration of other statically allocated objects, like drivers, threads, etc.

Since the order of static constructors is not defined, it is perfectly and legally possible that the constructor of the registrar will be invoked <b>after</b> the constructors of the objects that need to register into the list, thus the registrar must be guaranteed to be initialised <b>before</b> running any static constructors.

The solution is to design the object in such a way as to benefit from the standard <b>bss</b> initialisation, in other words take <code>nullptr</code> as starting values.

In practical terms, the list initialisation cannot be done in the constructor, but must be manually done before any method that adds elements to the list is called.

## Constructors

### static_double_list_links() {#a9748ad03de14f62527a68161210c3946}

<MemberDefinition
  prototype={<>micro_os_plus::utils::static_double_list_links::static_double_list_links ()</>}
 labels = {["constexpr"]}>
Construct a statically allocated list node (<b>bss</b> initialised).

As the name implies, it is assumed that the instance of the object is allocated statically and the entire content was set to zero during startup (via BSS init).

This is equivalent to setting the pointers to <code>nullptr</code>.

### ~static_double_list_links() {#abde78859511a6a64bf481128ed84cf87}

<MemberDefinition
  prototype={<>micro_os_plus::utils::static_double_list_links::~static_double_list_links ()</>}
 labels = {["constexpr"]}>
Destruct the node.

:::warning
The code to clear the pointers is now commented out, since recent GCC optimizes it out (dead store elimination). Depending on the version, there might be some attributes to allow this, but they are not safe, for example <br/>
<code>&#95;&#95;attribute&#95;&#95;((optimize(&quot;no-lifetime-dse,no-dse,no-inline&quot;)))</code> did not help. The workaround is to use <code><Link to="#ac7c7be24256a093ae9b047efd45cbfc3">nullify()</Link></code> explicitly, or, even better, to clear the memory before invoking the placement <code>new</code> constructor again.
:::

<MemberDefinition
  prototype={<>void micro_os_plus::utils::double_list_links_base::initialize_once (void)</>}>
Initialize the list only at first run.

<SectionUser title="Parameters">
None.
</SectionUser>

<SectionUser title="Returns">
Nothing.
</SectionUser>

If the statically allocated list is still in the initial <em>uninitialised</em> state (with both pointers <code>nullptr</code>), initialise the list to the empty state, with both pointers pointing to itself.

For non-statically initialised lists, this method is ineffective, since the node is always initialised at construct time.

:::info
This method must be manually called for statically allocated list before inserting elements, or performing any other operations.
:::
